column6: Both paragraphs convey the same theological concepts of being set apart for God, the transformative process of purification, and the role of the Spirit in sanctification, with only slight variations in wording.
column7: We were set aside, consecrated to God at salvation. Through the act of purifying our souls by the help of the Spirit we become transformed. This process of purification is what sanctifies us.
column8: At salvation we were set apart, dedicated to God. Through the work of cleansing our souls we are transformed with the help of the Spirit. This cleansing process is what sanctifies us.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same core message that while God provides guidance, individuals must actively engage in their own faith journey. The wording is slightly altered, but the doctrinal intent remains unchanged.

column6: The original paragraph refers to 'righteousness,' which has a specific theological connotation related to moral rightness, while the back-translated paragraph uses 'godliness,' which emphasizes piety and devotion. This change alters the doctrinal focus of the training process.
column7: How are we trained by righteousness? By being transformed through the renewal of our minds.
column8: How are we trained by godliness? By being transformed through the renewing of our minds.
